sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 46.6% a year from $6.91 billion in FY2017 to $215.9 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F211].
The path was not smooth: FY2020 fell 6.8% and FY2023 grew only 0.2%, while FY2024 and FY2025 rose 125.9% and 114.2% [D130][D284][D338][D393].
The FY2024 step change came from Data Center revenue up 217%, driven by Hopper GPU shipments for LLM training and inference [P22][P23].
FY2026 growth of 65.5% was driven by Blackwell data center compute and networking, with Data Center networking up 142% [D448][P8][P10].
Data Center was 89.7% of FY2026 revenue and contributed 60.2pp of the 65.5% growth [D620][D622][D448].
Within it, Compute contributed 46.1pp and Networking 14.1pp in FY2026 [D629][D636].
The filing attributes the increase to accelerated computing and AI platform shifts, with Blackwell the majority of Data Center revenue [P8][P10].
Operating income grew 60.1% against 65.5% revenue growth, an incremental margin of 57.3% [D449][D448][D475].
Diluted EPS rose 66.7% against 64.7% net income growth as the diluted share count fell 1.2% [D452][D450][D470].
Operating margin of 60.4% in FY2026 sits far above the 32.8% window median and just below the 62.4% FY2025 high [F50][D813][D812].
The FY2026 margin fell 2.0pp, with cost of revenue subtracting 3.9pp, partly offset by R&D and SG&A adding 1.3pp and 0.6pp [D463][D477][D478][D479].
The cost-of-revenue drag includes a $4.5 billion H20 excess inventory and purchase obligation charge in the first quarter [P7].
R&D and SG&A grew on compensation, employee growth and compute infrastructure, per the filing [P5][P4][P9].
Net margin of 55.6% trailed operating margin by 4.8pp, as other income of $11.1 billion partly offset a 15.1% tax rate [F70][F50][D861][X120][D434].
Operating cash flow of $102.7 billion was 0.86x net income, the window low against a 0.97x median [F100][F60][D435][D851].
Free cash flow of $96.7 billion was a 44.8% margin, near the 44.4% window median [F110][D432][D822].
Capex of $6.04 billion was 2.8% of revenue and 2.13x D&A, up from 1.74x in FY2025 [F105][F10][D431][D437][D382].
Inventory grew 112.3% and receivables 66.8%, both faster than revenue growth of 65.5% [D474][D473][D448].
Total debt was $8.47 billion against $10.6 billion of cash in FY2026 [D440][F150].
The FY2026 net-cash figure omits short-term investments, which were not reported that year, so the net-cash comparison across the gap is not like for like [R3].
Return on average equity of 101.5% ranks at the 100th percentile of six semis peers against a 20.3% median [D447][D848][D849].
Buybacks and dividends of $41.1 billion absorbed 42.5% of free cash flow, and the share count fell 1.2% [D443][D444][D470].
Short-term investments were not reported in FY2026 though reported in FY2025, so cash and investments and net cash omit them [R3][X188].
That data gap weakens any liquidity or net-cash conclusion drawn across the FY2025 to FY2026 boundary [R3].
Graphics was 44.1% of revenue and fell 25.0% in FY2023, a one-period cyclical drawdown [R1][D753][D754].
That decline reflected $2.17 billion of inventory provisions on excess Ampere Gaming and Data Center supply [P35][P38].
Product revenue members sum to 190% of consolidated FY2026 revenue, so they cannot be added [R2].
Operating margin: a print below the 62.4% FY2025 high would extend the FY2026 compression, reported in the FY2027 10-K [D812][F50].
Cash conversion: operating cash flow below 0.86x net income would mark a new window low, reported in the FY2027 10-K [D435].
Data Center share: a move below the 89.7% FY2026 level would signal the largest driver losing concentration, reported in the FY2027 10-K [D620].
